stem.text: A curve is defined by \( x = - 2 t^{2} + 4 t - 2 \) and \( y = 2 t^{3} + t^{2} + 1 \). Find \( \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \) at \( t = 2 \), and state whether the curve is concave up or concave down there.

answer_key.label: The curve is concave down at t = 2, because \( \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = - \frac{1}{8} \) there.

worked_solution.text: \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{6 t^{2} + 2 t}{4 - 4 t} \), which simplifies to \( \frac{- 3 t^{2} - t}{2 t - 2} \).
Differentiate with respect to t: \( \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = \frac{- 3 t^{2} + 6 t + 1}{2 t^{2} - 4 t + 2} \), which is \( \frac{1}{2} \) at \( t = 2 \).
Divide by \( \frac{dx}{dt} \), which is \( -4 \) at \( t = 2 \): \( \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = - \frac{1}{8} \), so the curve is concave down there.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative of a parametric curve

options.label: The curve is concave up at t = 2, because \( \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \frac{1}{2} \) there.
